summary: I fixed the two defects the code review sent back, each closed as a class with a committed corpus. O-030: suite_test.go now reads go test -json verdicts through a shared parse/judge (tests/acceptance/suite/judge_test.go), which keeps every pass, fail and skip at every level, subtests included. The Chrome check refuses any skip whose own output names CHROME_BIN, at any depth. It also refuses a browser test that passes while a subtest under it skipped. The no-browser check refuses a skipped subtest of a TestE00[1-6] test unless it is allow-listed. O-032: the assertion-site scanner now catches a non-zero return of any length, negative or in parentheses, with or without else, plus the bare exit()/quit() builtins. Widening it exposed exactly the two lines the review named (run_finish.py L145 and L184), and both now have Superseded rows. Both engine tests are committed as given and pass. Both real whole-suite checks still pass.

files.why: parse() keeps every verdict, subtests included. judgeWithout and judgeChrome are pure and judge those events. The file has no build tag, so its corpus runs under go test ./...

TestSuiteChecksReadEverySkip plants each corpus row into a healthy run and requires the judge to fire or stay quiet. The loader is strict: unknown keys, an empty corpus, bad mode/expect, duplicate names and placeholders are refused.
Corpus for O-030's class: 20 fire/quiet plant rows over subtest and nested-subtest skips in both modes, plus Browser's three message forms and the sibling-prefix and log-line quiet cases.
TestSuiteWithoutABrowser and TestSuiteInChrome now call parse plus the judges. The duplicated top-level-only logic is removed.
The engine's closing test for O-030, as given.
The site patterns now catch multi-digit, parenthesised and negative non-zero returns (bare and after else) and the exit()/quit() builtins. The Sites doc comment is updated to match.
Added rows RF-145 and RF-184 (run_finish.py's timeout verdict and its caller), both Superseded by go test -timeout.
The engine's closing test for O-032, as given.
TestSitesSeeEverySpelling holds Sites to every corpus row. The loader is strict: unknown keys, an empty corpus, missing sites, sites out of range and placeholders are refused.
Corpus for O-032's class: 48 rows of Python assertion-site spellings (fire) and look-alikes (quiet), each saying who writes it.

obligations.how:
parse() now keeps every pass, fail and skip at every level, keyed package/test.
- judgeChrome refuses any skip, subtest or nested subtest included, whose own output (its key and keys under key+'/') contains CHROME_BIN. It also refuses a browser test that passes while a subtest under it skipped.
- judgeWithout refuses a skipped subtest of a non-browser TestE00[1-6] test unless mayAlsoSkip lists its whole name.

Before the fix: run against judges that copied the old top-level-only logic, the corpus failed exactly 8 rows. These were the four Chrome subtest-skip rows (unset, nested, Edge message, no-file message), the browser-test-with-skipped-subtest row and the three no-browser acceptance-subtest rows. All 12 quiet and old-behaviour rows passed.

After the fix: all 20 rows pass.

The engine's TestSuiteInChromeRefusesASubtestSkipNamingChromeBin passes (48 s). Run by hand with the same overlay, the inner TestSuiteInChrome fails with '.../fakegithub/TestSC042SubtestSkipsForWantOfChromeBin/caller skipped saying CHROME_BIN with CHROME_BIN set'. That is also a measurement that test2json gives the skip message to the subtest. The real TestSuiteInChrome (279 top-level tests, nothing skipped) and TestSuiteWithoutABrowser (three browser skips, 16 acceptance passes, no subtest skips) both pass.

Widened the site patterns:
- `\breturn(?:\s+|\s*\()\s*(?:-\s*)?[1-9]\d*\b` catches `return 124, ...`, `return 10`, `return (1)`, `return(2)`, `return -1` and `return - 1`. It requires a space or '(' after return, so identifiers such as returned1 stay quiet.
- The else form now takes the same number grammar (`else 12`, `else -1`, `else (2)`).
- Added the bare `exit(`/`quit(` builtins. A preceding '.' or word character is excluded, so on_exit( and methods named exit stay quiet.

Before the fix: 13 corpus rows and the engine's TestSitesSeeMultiDigitExitCodes failed.

After the fix: all 48 rows pass, and so does the engine test. TestPortedAssertionsHaveAGoTest then reported exactly run_finish.py L145 and L184 as sites with no row. I added RF-145 and RF-184, both Superseded by go test -timeout, and the package passes. No other new sites appeared in the 12 snapshots. A code held in a variable (`return code`) is a known hole, pinned quiet in the corpus.

deviations: tests/acceptance/suite now has two untagged _test.go files (judge_test.go, corpus_test.go). The corpus therefore runs under plain go test -count=1 ./..., while the whole-suite runs stay behind sc042suite. As a result the suite package appears in untagged go test and go list output. It imports only the standard library, and TestAcceptanceLinksNoneOfTheProduct still passes.

Closing O-030 as a class went one member past the finding's text. In the Chrome run, a browser test that passes while a subtest under it skipped is now refused, because its top-level pass hides a part that never ran in the browser. No browser test has subtests today, so the real runs are unchanged.
Closing O-032 as a class added the bare exit()/quit() builtins to the site patterns besides the prescribed return/else widening. No snapshot uses them, so they exposed no new rows.
follow_ups: tests/acceptance/** (and now tests/acceptance/suite/testdata, tests/acceptance/ported/testdata/site_spellings.json) still has no owning block in the architecture record, since AA-043 was rejected. A person should decide which block, if any, owns the acceptance packages.
A known hole in Sites(), pinned quiet in site_spellings.json: an exit code held in a variable (`return code`) is not a site. Such verdicts are mapped only where a row is declared by hand.
